column1: # One row routes a recognized tool's output to an existing strategy, replacing
# a per-tool parser script. Consulted by the engine before strategy
# auto-detection (disable with --no-hints). First matching row wins.
#   tool        dataset/report name for the match (the tool's identity);
#               a family row may cover several tools with one shared name
#   match-type  prefix   — first non-blank input line starts with pattern
#               contains — pattern appears anywhere in the input
#               regex    — input matches the bash ERE pattern (anchor ^ = start
#   strategy    usually a generic strategy (strategies/delimited/ or
#               strategies/structured/); a bespoke target acts as detection
# Keep patterns structural (format shape), not sample-specific (literal names,
# dates, versions) — a row should also match UNSEEN output of the same tool.
# The corpus (tests/corpus/run.sh --golden) verifies rows do not misfire on
